crate_measured: tokenizers (real source files tokenizers/src/{ngram,edge_ngram,unicode_words}.rs via perf/bench #[path] include; simple_lowercase = tantivy SimpleTokenizer+LowerCaser, the pipeline SearchTokenizer::Simple builds)
rustc: 1.99.1 (RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.99.1; repo rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.100.0, overridden for this measurement)
environment: shared VM ~1.5 CPU, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2, release/bench profile, isolated CARGO_HOME under ~/workspace/perf-rollout/cargo-home-paradedb (shared ~/.cargo package-cache lock was held by a parallel rollout job)

inputs.short: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog (43 bytes)

notes: unicode_words/long_x10 is ~8.6x slower than simple_lowercase/long_x10 (294478.4 ns vs 34097.8 ns mean) in this run - real measured gap, worth profiling (per-bound emoji/unicode_words checks).
Criterion throughput figures in console output are not used: throughput was set on the group, so per-bench MiB/s is misleading; baseline uses time (ns) only.

Not covered: pg_search and all pgrx-based crates - this VM has no PostgreSQL/pg_config; full-workspace cargo resolution also requires fetching the datafusion git submodule, which timed out (>280s, and >1100s in the first attempt with shared cargo lock). Canonical in-crate bench tokenizers/benches/tokenizer_bench.rs is provided for a machine with the full toolchain.
Numbers are from a shared, throttled VM - treat as relative baseline for regression detection (>10% warn, >25% block), not absolute performance claims.
